newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian Moslem party delays election statement.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian Moslem party delays election statement.

text.p: Indonesia's Moslem-backed party said on Friday it was delaying a statement on whether it would accept last week's general election results due to the number of complaints of fraud from party branches around the country.
Leaders of the minority United Development Party (PPP), holding an extended meeting at a Jakarta hotel to review the election, said they would issue a statement on Saturday.
The 27-day campaign -- won by the ruling Golkar by a landslide -- saw the worst political violence in three decades, primarily between supporters of the PPP and Golkar.
Political and financial analysts have expressed concern over a possible recurrence of violence if PPP partisans feel they were cheated at the polls.

The PPP had earlier planned a statement on Friday, but officials said they were still preoccupied with reports from the party's 27 provincial branches speaking of intimidation and terror ahead of the election and on polling day.

"This (delay) happens because the meeting cannot end as scheduled on Friday. The meeting is tough and there are lobbies among chairmen of the party's branches. We have also heard reports and suggestions from the 27 branches," PPP secretary-general Tosari Widjaja said in a statement.
The PPP, which won just under just 23 percent of the vote, has alleged widespread electoral irregularities.

Golkar, in power for much of President Sujarto's 30-year rule, won more than 74 percent of the vote. The fragmented Indonesian Democratic Party (PPP) took three percent of the vote, which was for the 425 elected seats at the House of Representatives.
The PDI and independent monitors have also alleged irregularities in the campaign and poll, which is held every five years.
PPP officials have said there were signs of "vote buying" in some government offices dominated by Golkar.
